explanations.text:
●  you ask for something                              ([the front door](main))
  │     You type one line and press enter:
  │     human map server.py --verbatim abstraction.txt
  │     The tool reads the line, keeps what you want done
  │     and which file to do it to, and hands the ask
  │     to the hand that does that work.
  │
  ●  the tool guards your words                          ([the guard](cmd_map_h))
  │     Your words wait in abstraction.txt, exactly as you typed them.
  │     The guard takes the telling with the pins in it,
  │     strips the pins out, and compares what is left
  │     against your file, character for character.
  │     One changed word and the tool stops; nothing is written.
  │
  ●  the telling goes onto the map                    ([the map run](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py))
        When the words pass, the guard hands the pinned telling
        to the map run, which ties every pin to real lines
        and adds one entry to the map of the file.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  the tool finds the code files                      ([the sweep](scan_files))
     It walks the folder, keeps the files it can read as code,
     and drops hidden files, build folders, and any folder
     that already holds a map of its own.

  the tool checks the ignore list                    ([the sieve](is_ignored))
     It holds a file against the ignore list of the map:
     a name in the list covers that file, everything under it,
     and any file whose name fits the name as a pattern.

  the tool signs a project in                         ([the register](cmd_init))
     You type: human init hello_server.
     The tool makes a human folder in the project, puts the
     reader's own files into it, and writes the code files
     into the book the reader opens: human/human.json.

  the tool builds the map afresh                        ([the rebuild](fresh_map))
     It reads the map the project keeps, sweeps the folder
     again, and keeps only the files the sieve lets through,
     so a new file shows in the reader without a new init.

  the tool opens the reader                           ([the shelf](cmd_serve))
     You type: human serve. The tool finds the top of the
     project and gives its files to a browser, fresh on
     every ask and quiet unless you add --log.

  the tool hands the skills out                      ([the giver](cmd_skills))
     It copies every skill folder, and the shapes with it,
     into the place where your agent looks for skills.

  every other ask goes to the engine                 ([the engine](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py))
     Retext, undo, show, lines, and sync are the engine's work.
     This file only opens the door and points the way.

●  you open the door                                    ([the shelf](cmd_serve))
  │     You type: human serve.
  │     The tool climbs to the top of the project — the folder
  │     that holds human/ — so the command works from any
  │     folder inside the project.
  │     Then it takes door 8010 of your machine and stands there.
  │
  ●  the browser knocks                             ([the fresh copy](FreshHandler))
  │     You open http://localhost:8010/human/web.html.
  │     Each thing on the page — the reader, the maps, the code —
  │     is one knock: "give me this file".
  │     The tool hands out only files under the top of the
  │     project, never anything above it.
  │
  ●  every answer says: do not keep me                    ([the note](end_headers))
  │     The tool marks each file it hands out, so the browser
  │     asks fresh next time instead of showing an old copy.
  │     This is why a changed map shows up on a plain reload.
  │
  ●  the tool stands at the door until you stop it
        Ask after ask, it answers. Ctrl-c closes the door.
        Serving only reads; nothing in the project changes.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  when you want to see the asks                           ([the mute](log_message))
     human serve --log writes one line per knock.
     Without it the tool stays silent, because one page load
     is many knocks and they would flood your screen.

  when a second project wants a door
     A machine gives each numbered door to one program only,
     and the first serve holds door 8010. Give the second
     project its own door: human serve --port 8011, and read
     it at http://localhost:8011/human/web.html.
